title: Going back to the upright bass
summary: Having played electric only for others, Monk bought an upright to find out where he stood, contrasting Wes's guitar.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So we had a brand new station wagon and we were ready to go out as the Montgomery Brothers. Now, this is the interesting period because, I'm saying, finally, 'Well, I'm going back to the upright bass.'

It was just a natural thing that came. Because I wasn't...I had to find out for myself. I had to know for myself where I stood. I'm playing the electric bass in the beginning because of Hamp, and each period after that it was because of somebody else. It was never because of me.

Right, and rightfully so in some periods and points. Like with the Mastersounds, it was very natural for that sound. You see, it wasn't just a selfish thing by another person; it was a very natural sound. But I wanted it for myself. I had to go back and find for myself where I stood with the upright bass. Because I still had strong feelings for it, so I had to find out.

Now, because of me being who I am, I can't tear myself between two, whether it's instruments or people or whatever it is. I had to make a commitment to one. In other words, I couldn't pick the upright bass up and be true to it and still playing the electric bass. I had to go with one or the other. I have to make a total commitment to whatever I'm involved with.
I was ready for it mentally, and I thought I was ready for it physically. So I bought me an upright. I don't know; the old upright I had from some time back at home got stolen, or something...
So you hadn't had one for quite a while; you hadn't played one for a while?
We're going, now, since when I first started, when I left with Hamp...

Yeah. I hadn't played it since then; it's a long time. But the feeling was there and I had to find out what that is, find out where I stand, find out my own self. Is that a choice I want to make. And by '62 or '63, electric bass is beginning to come in a little bit more in its own.

I was by no means the only electric bass player around, fight? But I thought also, it would be a contrast of sound with Wes playing the guitar. I just had...it just made it more, my feeling more solid about I had to get back in the upright, into the other contrast, away from the string sound, the electric string sound, to the upright string sound.
I bought me an upright bass, a good bass. Our first job, as I recall, was back East at the Five Spot.
